1f762ed8c1: Build00:20–00:55 Where the piano came from
682d5c8cf6: Pianoforte: an instrument that can play "soft" and "loud"
bb25df8889: The harpsichord plucks its strings, so the volume can't change with your touch.
fa515142e4: The Italian Bartolomeo Cristofori took the harpsichord as a model and switched to hammers striking the strings, making an early piano "with soft and loud".
ce0549edac: The full name is pianoforte, "soft-loud". For convenience the forte, meaning loud, was dropped, leaving just piano.
8ac5b5a408: With its wide range and the ability to play melody and harmony together, it became the most important instrument for composing and music education.
e2e438dcf4: BuildHow it's built and makes sound
6f04adaf6a: Press a key and a hammer strikes the strings
165980fe83: Upright piano cross-section: the key drives wooden levers, the hammer strikes the strings, and the vibration travels to the soundboard
260f1213fb: In principle it's a struck string instrument; because you play it through a keyboard, it's classed as a keyboard instrument
e0bf10af86: 88 keys, a range from A0 to C8, over seven octaves, tuned in twelve-tone equal temperament
09b7dd35ec: Over two hundred strings inside, with an iron frame taking their pull
db87044d52: Let go of a key and the damper stops the string vibrating straight away
70194d8cb3: The vibrating strings make the sound; the hammers strike them and the soundboard makes it louder.
68c3c9c796: The piano combines the principles of which two kinds of instrument?
7481fa83b6: Strings make the sound and hammers strike them, so the piano combines the principles of string and percussion instruments.
fe1201ab4c: From concert hall to bedroom: the keyboard family
4e57e9b305: A grand piano with its lid up, showing the strings and keyboard
788978312a: Strings lie horizontally and the hammers strike from below; a responsive touch, standard for concerts.
50d92ee838: A dark wooden upright piano with keys and pedals
7fd5aed39f: Strings stand vertically and the hammers strike from the front; compact, and most common in homes and classrooms.
3d14e1d9c7: An 88-key digital piano on an X stand
37ecdb4056: Samples a real piano's sound; you can practise with headphones and connect to a computer over MIDI.
0fb7a111a3: A keyboard synthesizer with a screen, knobs and buttons
47c4e0d683: 49 to 88 keys, with lots of built-in sounds and rhythms; light and easy to carry.
ed3ed6d20d: There are also silent pianos you can practise on with headphones, player pianos, and organs with two manuals plus a pedalboard. For a beginner, an instrument with at least 61 touch-sensitive keys is best.
2e4564e446: Pop piano is the foundation for jazz piano
4996793f49: Played from staff notation, with an emphasis on sight-reading and fine technical interpretation.
55b9f4b1d5: Accompanying freely from chord symbols, adding ornaments and fills, and pushing and laying back with syncopation for a pop feel.
b38fca00a5: Mostly improvised, with seventh chords and walking bass; play a song a hundred times and it's different every time.
aeaa73fb41: Ornaments and syncopation added to the original
a612e1bc29: Grooves from dances around the world
fda531d9b7: Listen to four piano pieces and guess the style of each
e6f79970bd: Ballade pour Adeline and 不能說的秘密 are pop piano: a clear melody over mostly broken-chord accompaniment. Bill Evans and Oscar Peterson are jazz piano: rich harmony, with the melody improvised again and again.

1b9e33d875: Sit steady and relaxed, fingers as if holding a ball
5d3db5891e: Sit on the front half of the bench, centred on middle C, feet flat on the floor
fba65a8840: Bench height: elbows roughly level with the keys
69f219c493: Shoulders relaxed, upper arms hanging naturally, wrists neither sagging nor raised

1270cc07ea: Loose shoulders, level elbows, straight wrists, round fingers
3ab8268aac: If your shoulders or wrists feel tight while playing, stop, shake out your hands and set your hand shape again. Playing slowly is fine; tension is what you most need to avoid.
c5b77f4087: The thumb is 1 and the little finger 5, on both hands
7508b4c5b3: Both hands resting in a natural curve on the keyboard, the left in the low register and the right in the high
81ab001bf7: Finger numbers: left hand 1 to 5 from thumb to little finger; right hand 1 to 5 from thumb to little finger
5cf948e141: This course writes accompaniment as "L5 L3 L2 L1" and "R1 R2 R5": L is the left hand, R the right, and the numbers are fingers.
2b95b2f261: Three pedals, each with a job
76c064d535: Pressing it lifts the dampers off the strings, so the sound keeps going after you let go of the keys. It's the one pop piano uses most; change the pedal when you change chords.
392c86b176: Makes the sound quieter and softer. On a grand it shifts the hammers; on an upright it moves the hammers closer to the strings.
7e370add7f: On a grand it sustains only certain notes; on an upright it's often a mute for quiet practice.
02c1f196e4: Right after you press the chord, lift the pedal and press it again, so the new chord is sustained and the old one is cut off. Remember: play, lift, press.
1ecfa73437: The white key left of a pair of black keys is C
e7a2971286: Black keys repeat in groups of two and three. The C nearest the middle of the piano is middle C (C4). The keys marked light blue are all Cs.
9fa6949c2e: You have to master classical piano before you can play pop
e42a5cc34f: MythPop piano starts from chords, so you can begin from zero; classical technique is a great help, though.
9b82827aea: The thinner the string, the lower the note
7d009ad6ae: MythThe thinner and shorter the string, the higher the note; bass strings are thick and long and wrapped in copper wire.
603e176bb0: FactStrings stretch over time and go out of tune; tune at least once a year.
55a3d5d855: Holding the sustain pedal down the whole time sounds best
f6f0b46f37: MythDifferent chords blur together into mud; change the pedal when you change chords.
88e77c9934: A piano doesn't like damp, or too dry either
408ab0d1c3: FactThe right environment is about 20°C with 50–60% humidity, out of direct sunlight.
51d075fcb0: You have to press hard for a good sound
e543cb12f1: MythLetting the arm's weight fall naturally is stronger than pushing the keys, and won't hurt you.
